Modals for Speculating in the Past
Modal verbs express different degrees of a possibility, ability, or necessity. Speculation of past events refers to the consideration of possibilities that did not materialize.
I must have been somewhat heedless during class.
Before then, web programming must have been a real brain-teaser.

At this point, you're already familiar with modal verbs and some of their common uses. Now, we will learn how to use them to speculate about past events. We will focus on three modal verbs frequently used for this purpose: should, could, must and may.

A speculation is a consideration of different possibilities in regards to an action or an event. Let's take a look at this scenario:
  • Person A: "The president of the company is not picking up the phone."
  • Person B: "He may still be in the meeting."

Person A provides a situation, and person B is speculating, or considering, one of the possible reasons for that situation. This example is expressed in the present tense. Now, let's focus on speculations about past events.

All past actions and events we speculate about are finished; that's why we use perfect tenses and past participle forms of the verbs. The basic structure for a speculation about the past is:

Subject + Modal verb + Have (perfect tense auxiliary) + Main verb (in past participle form) + Complement

Examples:
  • Person A: "This website is horribly programmed."
  • Person B: "Its programmers may have been in a hurry when they put it together."
  • Person C: "But, the software engineers were awarded with a quality bonus; they must have done a perfect job this year!"

As you can see, must and may have virtually the same meaning in the context of speculation about past events, as they both express a guess from the speaker. The modal verb should, however, is used to provide an opinion of what would have been a better alternative to the past action.

Example:
  • Person A: "I failed the final programming exam!"
  • Person B: "You should have reviewed the PHP video I sent you."

Person B knows that Person A did not review the video, and that may have helped Person A to pass the exam.
You may have heard of PHP 7.1, which is its last iteration.
Past, Present, and Future in Passive Form
The passive voice is useful when we want to talk about actions or events and we want to focus on them, instead of focusing on who performed or caused them.
PHP was created in 1994 by Rasmus Lerdorf.
You may have heard of PHP 7.1, which is its last iteration; it was released on December 2016, and will be supported until around 2020.

We can use the passive voice to:
  • Change the focus of the sentence.
  • Avoid mentioning the performer of the action because it is not important, or it's unknown.
  • Provide a sense of impersonality to a formal document (such as a research paper).

The verb to be is very important in the passive voice. Sometimes, however, it can be substituted by the verb get.

Now, we will review the forms of the passive voice, depending on the tense in which it is used.

Passive Voice in Past Tenses

The most common use of the passive voice in past is the expression of dates and authors of creations (books, machines, theories, etc.); this is done in past simple:

Active voice: Sir Isaac Newton proposed the theory of Universal Gravitation.
Passive voice: The theory of Universal Gravitation was proposed by Sir Isaac Newton.

Of course, the passive voice can be used in any other form of past, and it can get quite complex; let's take a look at the following chart to see some examples:

(The words in parentheses in the chart are optional, as they refer to the performer of the action)

Passive Voice in Present Tenses

Again, the passive voice is very useful in this tense, and it can be used in any form, whenever the performer of the action is not relevant.

{"rows":4,"columns":2,"cells":["{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"Active Voice\"}","{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"Passive Voice\"}","{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"We use PHP every day at the office.\"}","{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"PHP is used every day at the office (by us).\"}","{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"We are using PHP to design websites more easily.\"}","{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"PHP is being used to design websites more easily.\"}","{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"The company has implemented PHP as standard in all branches.\"}","{\"type\": \"text\", \"content\": \"PHP has been implemented as standard in all branches (by the company).\"}"],"styles":" intro_table_border instruction_table_background"}

Passive Voice in Future Tenses

Some of the common uses of the passive voice in future tenses are the assignment of deadlines, warning of future changes in procedures, and reporting of future events. Using the passive voice in contexts like these provides a degree of formality and impersonality: what matters is the action/event, not who will do it.

Juan: Hello, Gabriel! What are you doing?
Gabriel: Hi! I'm reviewing my notes about PHP but they weren't written very clearly. I must have been somewhat heedless during class.
Juan: Oh! Let me help you! Let's review PHP together.
Gabriel: Great, thanks!
Juan: The basics should be covered first. What's PHP?

Gabriel: It was defined in the classroom as an open-source scripting language; PHP stands for Hypertext Processor. But the definition of open-source was not explained in class.
Juan: Open-source software is software that can be obtained for free and is made available to anyone.
Gabriel: Thanks! I may have taken some additional notes, let me see… Okay, PHP has been widely adopted because of its great compatibility; using this powerful language, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and plain text can be integrated with a single platform. This wide compatibility must have been revolutionary in programming!
Juan: I'm sure it was! No wonder it's so popular these days. You know that the cloud will be the future of data storage and movement, and the code used by PHP is executed directly on the server. I'm sure this language will be used by everyone in the future!

Gabriel: This is the first programming language I have studied, and I cannot imagine how difficult it may have been to create dynamic content without it. PHP was created in 1994 by Rasmus Lerdorf; before then, web programming must have been a real brain-teaser.
Juan: Yes! The current popularity of web programming as a career may have been the result of the versatility and flexibility of PHP. The process of designing a website was simplified a lot with it! PHP can be executed on virtually any OS, any server type you can come across, and the format of your input ranges from plain text to HTML, to even Flash movies! You may have heard of PHP 7.1, which is its last iteration; it was released in December 2016 and will be supported until around 2020.
Gabriel: Yes! That's the one being discussed in the course. PHP must have changed a lot since it was released back in the 90s!
